the battle, called from the map's $0CAB with the two sides' units in $038A-$038F: sets the machine up ($87B5) and the map's sound player ($F128), seeds the random numbers from the raster line ($D012, $D011) and runs them a random number of times, clears the sprite list ($905E, $8DFA, $8CBC), unpacks one of the three battlefields ($90A5) and scatters its scenery ($913F), turns the screen on (multicolour bitmap, $3B), starts the raster interrupts ($9018), draws the players' unit icons ($9176), then for each side brings on its infantry ($9423), cavalry ($9479) and cannon ($94D2) and saves the strip under its range gauge ($8E85); clears the lanes ($A8E3).

the battle's main loop, one side a pass ($85DD flipped each time): the unit chosen ($9781), the keys ($888C, kept in $89D1), the stick or keys of a person ($979D), the choice of unit ($96F7), falling back ($A7A8), the orders ($9805), the cannon's animation ($9DE0), the cannon's moves ($9E37), the infantry's moves and pictures ($9E0D), the cannon's pictures ($966E), the cavalry's ($95A0), the ravine and river ($A113), the cannonballs landing ($A5D3), new units for the gaps ($A7F6), the end of the battle ($A869) and a cannon hit ($A62C); then sound 13 for a hit ($87A2) and sound 3 or 17 for the cavalry's charge ($87A3).

the charge's sound: while it plays ($87A3), sound 17 once both sides' cavalry are gone ($038C + $038D) or neither is moving ($8614 + $8615); otherwise sound 3 starts when some cavalry is moving and one of the six riders has a picture ($833F).
the end of the battle, from $A88E: the raster interrupt off and acknowledged, the screen blanked ($D011 bit 4 clear), and the two pla drop $A869's return so that the rts goes back to the map.

code nothing in the battle calls: it makes port B of CIA 2 an input, compares bit 2 of $DD00 with bit 3 and, when they differ, turns the interrupts off and jumps to $CE00. With $CE00 it looks like the developers' link to another computer over the user port, left in memory when the file was saved.

the battle's machine: RAM with I/O ($35), the CIA interrupts and timers off, $0392-$0395 cleared (nobody fell back or lost yet), video bank 1 ($DD00 = 2), black border and background, sprites off, bitmap at $4000 and screen at $6000 ($D018 = $80), the screen blanked ($2F), 40 columns of multicolour ($D016 = $18), the raster interrupt off, the 32 sprite slots in order with their places at 0, sprite multicolours $0A and 0, and NMI and reset pointing at the rti at $884C.

the keys of the side this pass, as a code in A (and $89D1): for the Union RUN/STOP (4: choose the next unit) and E (6: fall back), for the Confederacy F5 (5) and the up-arrow (7); H, for either, pauses ($8907); $FF for none. Each row's choice is checked by reading $DC00 back, so a joystick in port 2 holding a line low cannot fake a key.

H: unless the last pause ended less than 50 frames ago ($893F), sound 17, the pause flag on ($893E, which stops the moving and the timers in the interrupt), 50 frames' wait ($893F), then a wait for H again, 50 more frames before H counts again, the flag off and the charge sound's flag cleared ($87A3).

the raster interrupt at line $E0, below the field (and line $F9 the first time, $9018): sets the next one for line 0 ($8A2B), copies the sprite list into the live tables ($8DFA) and sorts it ($8CBC), lets interrupts in again, and unless the game is paused ($893E) moves the shots into the sprite list ($A521), counts the timers down ($87A7), steps the random numbers ($9073), moves the shots ($A5A3) and counts the two frame counters ($87A0, $87A1); plays the sound unless it is being started ($A909, $F12E); counts the pause timer down ($893F).

the raster interrupt at line 0: the first seven sprites of the sorted list ($8CE7) on hardware sprites 1 to 7 (place, high bit of x, pointer, colour), then the next interrupt 21 lines below the first one's top ($8A9A), or the bottom one ($8B32) when that is past line $D6.

unpacks from ($10) to ($12) until the count in $14/$15 goes below zero, so one byte more than the count: each control byte gives eight flags, top bit first; a 1 copies the next byte, a 0 takes the next byte as a count and writes the last byte copied that many times.
saves the strip of eight cells the side's range gauge is drawn on ($8EB9): 64 bytes of bitmap, 8 of screen and 8 of colour, into the store at $CC57 (the Union) or $CCA7 (the Confederacy).

the side's gauge pointers: $40 the strip's bitmap ($824E: $4180 for the Union, $4200 for the Confederacy, row 1), $42 its store ($8256), $48 and $44 its screen and colour bytes ($8252, colour $7800 above).
the side's gauge empty: its bitmap cleared, its screen bytes $BC and colours white, when a cannon starts to aim ($A505).

the side's gauge for its range ($8260, 0 to 31): eight cells of the lozenge pattern ($8263), four pixel pairs to a cell, filled from the left for the Union and from the right for the Confederacy, the cell at the end shifted by $825C.
the side's gauge put back ($8FC2 with X its side times two), once the cannon has fired.
the strip X/2's bitmap, screen and colour bytes back from their store ($8E85); also from $A651 when a person's aiming cannon is hit.
the raster interrupt on, at $89D5 for line $F9, after the frame's bottom; all eight sprites on, sprite 0 multicolour, none stretched.
the 32 slots of the sprite list put out of sight (y $E8, pointer $E0, a blank image), and $826C cleared.
the next random number in A: the sum of $90A0, $90A3, $90A4 and 1, with the five bytes at $90A0-$90A4 shifted along.
the random sum being made.
the five bytes the random numbers come from, newest first; they start as the text "random" with $909F.
rnd_seed, continued: the second byte, moved on to $90A2 by each step.
rnd_seed, continued: the third byte, moved on to $90A3.
rnd_seed, continued: the fourth byte, added in and moved on to $90A4; seeded from the raster line ($D012) by $8007.
rnd_seed, continued: the fifth and last byte, added in; seeded from $D011 by $800D.

picks the battlefield with a random number ($826D): below $55 the canyon with its wooden bridge (1), below $AA the river with its stone bridge (2), otherwise the open field (0); unpacks its bitmap to $4000 ($826E) and its screen to $6000 ($8274), and its colours to $D800 ($827A), or for the open field colour RAM all green (5).

on the open field and the river, not the canyon: each of places 0 to 7 (four at the top, four at the bottom) gets, with a random number below $7F, a random one of the field's four ($8288): the house (picture 0), one of the two trees (3, 4) or nothing; the picture kept in $8280.
the scenery place field_scenery is on: the operand of the ldx at $9170, written at $9166.
the unit each person has chosen, as an icon: the Union's (pictures 21-23) at place 8, top left, the Confederacy's (24-26) at place 9, top right; nothing for a side the computer plays.
the screen and colour bytes of the Confederacy's three icons (pictures 24 to 26), inside the code: grey where the Union's are blue.

redraws every object slot whose redraw flag is set ($83AB), from slot 39 down: builds the picture's mask ($9341); if the slot was drawn, covers it with sprite 0 ($A317) and puts back the background it saved ($92BF); a slot marked to go ($852E = 0) is emptied; otherwise works out its new place ($91FD), saves the background there ($9247) and draws the mask ($93A4); then sprite 0 off ($A36D).
the slot draw_objects is on, from 39 down: the operand of the ldy at $91B6, written at $91B3, $91F7.

slot Y's bitmap address ($20/$21, kept in $84B6/$84DE): cell row y / 8 ($8571, $8558) and column x / 4 ($85B2, $858A) into the bitmap at $4000, the line in the cell (y and 7) in $85DA and $8506; x from $94 up is off the field, so the slot is marked undrawn ($8506 = $FF), sprite 0 goes off and the two pla skip the drawing.

saves the bitmap bytes under slot Y's picture (bitmap AND the picture's pixels) into its store under the I/O chip ($8466/$848E: $D000 + 84 x slot, written with $01 = $34): four columns of 21 lines, stepping into the next cell row after a cell's eighth line.
the low byte of the store save_under writes: the low byte of the address of the sta at $9278, written at $924D.
the high byte of the store save_under writes: the high byte of the address of the sta at $9278, written at $9253.
the end of save_under's column, 21 more for each column: the operand of the cpx at $9291, written at $9265, $92A8.
the column save_under is on, as an offset of 8 a column: the operand of the adc at $9298, written at $9260, $92B1.
Y kept by save_under: the operand of the ldy at $92B8, written at $9247.
ORs slot Y's saved bytes back into the bitmap at its old place ($84B6/$84DE, line $8506), the picture's pixels gone again.
the low byte of the store restore_under reads: the low byte of the address of the lda at $92F3, written at $92C5.
the high byte of the store restore_under reads: the high byte of the address of the lda at $92F3, written at $92CB.
the end of restore_under's column: the operand of the cpx at $9310, written at $92E5, $932A.
the column restore_under is on, as an offset of 8 a column: the operand of the adc at $9317, written at $92EA, $9333.
Y kept by restore_under: the operand of the ldy at $933A, written at $92BF.

the mask for picture $8557 in the 84 bytes at $83D3 (four columns of 21 lines, all $FF to start): each of the picture's 63 bytes ($6400 + 64 x picture, from $8297 and $82E5), inverted, at its place ($8427), then all shifted right by x and 3 pixel pairs with 1s coming in, so the picture sits at the slot's exact place.
the low byte of the picture build_mask reads: the low byte of the address of the lda at $9363, written at $934A.
the high byte of the picture build_mask reads: the high byte of the address of the lda at $9363, written at $9350.
Y kept by build_mask: the operand of the ldy at $93A1, written at $9341.
ANDs the mask into the bitmap at the slot's new place: the picture's pixel pairs, all %11, become %00, the black background, so every soldier, horse and cannon on the field is a black figure.
the end of draw_mask's column: the operand of the cpx at $93D8, written at $93AE, $93EF.
the column draw_mask is on, as an offset of 8 a column: the operand of the adc at $93DF, written at $93B3, $93F8.

a random one of the side's four lanes ($869A + 4 x side) not taken yet, marked taken, its height in $8699 ($86A2: $23, $37, $55, $73 for the Union, $28, $4B, $69, $82 for the Confederacy); a new unit's soldiers are placed from it.

a lane ($9400) and, if the side has infantry ($038A), up to six soldiers at their places in it ($85DE x, $85EA + lane y), past the side's own edge: the Union's left, the Confederacy's right; their death counters cleared, the line marching on ($8612 = 1, $864C = 1) the way of the enemy ($8789), in formation 0, not reforming.

a lane and up to three riders ($038C) at their places ($85F6, $85FC + lane), past the side's edge, walking on ($8614 = 1, $8680 = 1) toward the enemy, in line (formation 0), not turning, the computer's plan at 0 ($8796).
the side's cannons ($038E) into its reserve ($8610), then the first one ($94DB).

if a cannon is left in reserve ($8610): one fewer there, and the cannon at its place ($8602, $8604 + lane) past the side's edge with nine shots ($8608), moving on ($8616 = 1, $8696 = 1) toward the enemy ($8692).

every 10 frames ($9E33): each of the side's six soldiers: a falling one ($8618) shows its two falling pictures ($8644 + 0, + 1), then is marked to go ($852E = 0) and the side's infantry count ($038A) drops by one; the others take the picture of the line's state: walking ($8642 + frame $864A) while it marches or falls back, standing ($8640) when it stands, aiming ($8654) then firing ($8660) when it fires; a changed picture sets the slot's redraw flag; then the slots are redrawn ($91B1).

every 6 frames ($86AE): the frame count ($8676) on, the riders moved ($9FD2), the end of falling back checked ($A2E0); then each of the side's three riders: a hit one ($8624, 2 to 9, then 8 and 9 again) shows the fall and the riderless horse ($8672 + counter - 2); falling back, the walk of the other side's riders, which face the other way ($866E of the other side); otherwise by the cavalry's state: standing ($866C), walking ($866E + frame), charging ($8670 + frame 0 to 3, then 2 and 3 again, with its hits, $A655), rearing ($8672 + frame); then the slots are redrawn.

each pass, for the side's cannon (unless gone, $8790): hit ($862A), three pictures ($868A + counter - 2) and then the slot emptied ($8345 = $FF) and the side's cannon count ($038E) one fewer; moving or leaving, the sideways pictures ($8684 + frame $868C) or, going up or down, the end-on ones ($8686); standing ($8682); aiming, standing until it fires and then the shot ($8688 + frame); then the slots are redrawn.

a person's choose key (RUN/STOP for the Union, F5 for the Confederacy, $89D1), with the stick still and fire not pressed and 12 frames since the last ($86AA): the infantry on the field stops ($8612 = 0), the next unit chosen ($8295: infantry, cavalry, cannon, round), sound 5, units the side has none of passed over ($9748), and the icon drawn ($9176).

moves the side's choice ($8295) on past a unit it has none of: infantry with $038A at 0, cavalry with $038C at 0, a cannon that is hit or not there ($862A) with no cannon in reserve. The reserve is read as $8610 for both sides, the Union's, so the Confederacy keeps a missing cannon chosen while the Union has one in reserve; its orders then do nothing ($9982).
the side's choice checked again ($9748); when it moved, because the unit was lost, 12 frames' delay and the icon redrawn.
the unit chosen before unit_check looked again: the operand of the cmp at $9790, written at $9787.

the stick or keys of a person into $89D2-$89D4: nothing when the computer plays both sides; with two people, the Union on the joystick in port 2 and the Confederacy in port 1; with one, the joystick in port 2, or with the keyboard chosen on the menu ($0388): Z left, X right, P up, L down, space fire ($8940).

the side's orders this pass: a side that fell back ($0392) stops its cannon; the computer's side ($0382) plans its own ($9A24); a person's chosen unit takes the stick: the cavalry ($98C5), the cannon ($9978), or the infantry here: nothing while it marches on, falls back, fires or reforms; fire: reform into formation 0 first ($A376), then fire ($A384); the stick still: stand; left or right: march that way, toward the enemy at once, away only in formation 1 (reforming first), not past an edge it has reached ($8706-$870C); up or down: march that way.

a person's cavalry: nothing while it rides on, falls back or turns ($8680, $860C, $867A); fire: from file (formation 1) turn back into line ($A3FD), otherwise charge forward ($A43E); the stick still: once moving it walks on toward the enemy ($8704); sound 2 when it starts; forward: charge; backward: from line into file ($A3FD), or in file, or alone, rear ($A450); up or down: walk that way unless at the edge ($870E, $8710).

a person's cannon: nothing while it rolls on, has no shots, is hit or leaves; aiming: until it fires, fire held raises the range ($8260) by one every four frames ($87A0) up to 31, drawn on the gauge ($8EFE), and three passes after fire is let go ($8694) it fires ($868E, $A567) and the gauge goes back ($8FBD); not aiming: fire starts the aim ($A4EC); up or down moves it unless at the edge ($8712, $8714); the stick still stops it, facing the enemy.
the computer's side: its cannon ($9C72), cavalry ($9B40), infantry ($9A78), and whether to fall back ($9A34).

falls back ($A7C1) with about one chance in 500 a pass (a random number of 0, then one from $7F up) when it has a territory to go to ($0390), its units have all arrived, it is down to three soldiers and riders or fewer and the enemy has at least as many (the cmp at $9A62).
the computer's own soldiers and riders, which the enemy's must reach for it to fall back: the operand of the cmp at $9A62, written at $9A52.

the computer's line, once on the field and not falling back: stands while any of its three bullets flies; otherwise takes its first standing soldier ($9B2D) and the nearest enemy across ($9D88); with none, or the enemy behind, stands; more than 3 lines above or below, marches up or down (or forward at an edge); level with it, stands and, within 30 pixel pairs and with its level's chance ($9D14), fires; farther, marches forward.
the side's infantry stands ($8612 = 0).
X the side's first standing soldier, from slot 11 down ($862C sides, $8618 counters), $FF when there is none.

the computer's cavalry, by its plan ($8796): 0, with its level's chance ($9D14) and sound 2: on the open field straight to plan 5; at a bridge into file ($A3FD), plan 1; 1 and 4: wait for the turn to end; 2: up or down to the bridge's height ($879A: $50 on the canyon, $37 on the river), and there charge across, plan 3; 3: once across (x $5A or more for the Union, below $37 for the Confederacy) back into line, plan 4; 5: up or down toward the nearest enemy ($9D30) and, within four lines of it, charge, plan 6; 6: the charge rides on.
code nothing reaches, after the jmp at $9C4B: the cavalry walking forward ($8614 = 1, direction $8789), where plan 6 charges instead.
the side's cavalry stands ($8614 = 0).
X the side's first standing rider, from 5 down ($8638 sides, $8624 counters), $FF when there is none.

the computer's cannon, when on the field, standing or moving, its ball not flying and its delay over ($8792): takes the nearest enemy up or down ($9D30); 8 lines or more away it moves toward it; nearer it stops and, with a random number below $14 and its level's chance ($9D14), aims at it: the range is the distance across / 4 - 1 (giving up past 31), the delay 10, and it fires ($A567).
the computer's chance by the level chosen for its side ($0380): 0 goes on only with a random number below 12 (12 in 256), 1 below 25, 2 always; when it fails, the two pla end the caller's pass.

the enemy object nearest up or down to height A: of the 20 slots, the other side's with a picture, not falling and between x 5 and $90; its slot in X and $878F ($FF none), the distance in $878E, its y in A.
the enemy object nearest across to x A, as $9D30; its x in A.
the side's cannon frame ($9DE4).
every 10 frames ($86B6): the cannon's frame flips ($868C); when it is back at 0 after the shot, the cannon stands again.
every 10 frames ($86AC): the infantry moves ($9EC5), its frame flips ($864A) and a firing line whose frame is back at 0 stands again; then its pictures ($9519).
the side's cannon moves ($9E43) unless the side fell back.

every 10 frames ($86B4), a cannon not hit: leaving, two pixel pairs a step toward its own edge; moving, by its direction ($8692): up 4 lines (stopping above $10, $8712), right 2, down 4 (up to $AA, $8714), left 2; then whether it has left ($A1F3) or arrived ($A232).

a line that marches or falls back, or reforms ($9F69): each standing soldier by the line's direction ($8648): up 3 lines (stopping below $0A, $8706), right 2 pixel pairs (flagging $870C from $8C), down 3 (to $AA, $8708), left 2 (flagging $870A below $10); the flags stop the next order that way, not this walk; then whether the line has gone ($A2AB) or arrived ($A262).

one of six steps: each standing soldier moves by its offsets ($86BC/$86C8 out of formation 0, $86D4/$86E0 out of 1); after the sixth the formation flips ($8646) and the reform ends ($864E). Formation 0 is three rows of two, 12 lines apart; formation 1 two rows of three.

arrival first ($867E): the cavalry stands and has arrived; then each rider: a riderless horse (counter 8 or more) runs on, 3 pixel pairs a step, the Union's right and the Confederacy's left; a standing rider, when the cavalry walks, charges or falls back: by its direction ($8678) up 3 lines (above $10, $870E), right, down 3 (to $AA, $8710) or left, 2 pixel pairs a step walking and 3 charging, with the edges checked ($A462, $A495); then a turn's step ($A0AA).

one of eight steps: each standing rider moves by its offsets ($86EC/$86F2 from line, $86F8/$86FE from file); after the eighth the formation flips ($8674) and the turn ends ($867A). In line the three ride one above another, 16 lines apart; in file they ride in a row at the top one's height, 8 pixel pairs apart, which fits on a bridge.

on the canyon and the river: each of the 20 objects standing, or a riderless horse, whose cell row ($8383 / 8) has a hazard column (the canyon's table at $876C, the river's at $8752; $FF where the bridge is) with its x / 4 from that column to 3 more falls in: a standing one falls (counter 1); a horse is gone (counter $0B, marked to go), its side's cavalry count one fewer and, at 0, its cavalry stands.

bullet X (0-2 the Union's, 3-5 the Confederacy's) against the enemy's objects: one with a picture and standing, with the bullet from 8 pixel pairs before its x to its x and 4 lines either side of its y, falls (counter 1); the bullet is spent, the hit sound's flag set ($87A2), a cannon hit noted ($87A4, $87A5).

a leaving cannon ($860A) past the edge (x from $A0 to $EF): its slot emptied; with its side not fallen back and a cannon in reserve, the next one comes on ($A8E3, $94DB); otherwise the cannon is done ($8790 = $FF) and its flags cleared.
an arriving cannon ($8696): the Union's once x is from $0C to $9F, the Confederacy's once below $8B: it stops and has arrived.

an arriving line ($864C): the Union's once its first standing soldier (from 5 down) is from x $20 to $9F, the Confederacy's once below $78: it stands and has arrived; the Union's right edge flag cleared.
a line falling back once none of its soldiers is drawn ($8506, $850C): no longer falling back, standing, and counted as off the field ($864C = 1), so it takes no more orders.
the same for the riders ($8512, $8515): no longer falling back, standing, off the field ($8680 = 1); the two pla end $95A0's pass.

hardware sprite 0, black, with slot Y's picture (pointer $90 + picture) at the slot's new place (x x 2 + 24, y + 50), over the object while its bitmap is redrawn; from x $94 sprite 0 goes off instead ($A36D).
sprite 0 off.
the line starts to reform ($864E = 1, $8650 = 0), marching pictures ($8612 = 1).

the line fires ($8612 = 2, frame 0): of each pair of soldiers (slots 0-1, 2-3, 4-5 of the side's six) the first standing one fires a bullet ($A3CB); a pair with neither standing has its bullet spent; sound 6.
bullet Y from soldier X: x the soldier's + 8 (the Union) or - 8 ($8746), y the soldier's - 2, a life of 15 frames ($8736).
X kept by bullet_start, the soldier: the operand of the ldx at $A3D8, written at $A3CE.
the line marches ($8612 = 1) in direction A ($8648), its frame kept at 0 or 1.

unless turning already: counts the side's riders drawn on the field ($8512 or $8515, into the operand at $A42A); none: the two pla end the caller's pass; one: returns, as one rider has no formation; two or three: the turn starts ($867A = 1, step 0) and the two pla end the caller's pass.
the side's riders drawn on the field, counted by cavalry_turn_start: the operand of the lda at $A429, written at $A404, $A414, $A41D, $A426.
the cavalry charges ($8614 = 2, frame 0), unless it is already.
the cavalry rears ($8614 = 3).
the cavalry's direction A ($8678), frame kept at 0 or 1.

after rider X moved left (its x in A): an arriving rider from $86 to $8A means the cavalry has arrived ($867E); past the left edge (from $F5) the rider is moved $3C on, out of sight beyond the right edge, a riderless horse is lost ($A4CC), and the cavalry rides on again ($8680), its plan at 0, turning back into line if in file.

after rider X moved right: an arriving rider from $0F to $13 means the cavalry has arrived; past the right edge ($96 to $9F) the rider is moved $3C on, out of sight beyond the left edge, a riderless horse is lost, and the cavalry rides on again as at $A462. A charge that crosses the field comes back in from its own side.
rider X a riderless horse (counter 8 or more) not yet marked: marked to go ($853A = 0), the side's cavalry count one fewer, and the two pla end the edge check at once, so it does not come back.
the cannon aims ($8616 = 2): range 0 ($8260), the frame count cleared ($87A0), not fired, the gauge empty ($8EE4), the range timer at 4 ($86B2).
Y kept by cannon_aim: the operand of the ldy at $A508, written at $A502.
the cannon moves ($8616 = 1) in direction A ($8692), its frame kept at 0 or 1.

the eight shots into sprite slots 0-7 of the list: x x 2 + 24 with its high bit, y + 50, pointer $DE + kind ($8726: $DE the bullet, $DF the cannonball), black; a spent shot ($872E negative) gets the blank image ($E0) at y $EE, out of sight.

sound 4; the side's ball (shot 6 + side) from the cannon's mouth (x + 4 or - 2, $8794) at its y, its life (range + 2) x 2 frames ($873C); one shot fewer ($8608), and after the ninth the cannon leaves the field ($860A), its direction 1 or 3 for the sideways pictures.

each frame, from the interrupt: each live shot: a bullet's hits ($A18F), then x by its speed ($873E: bullets 3 a frame, balls 2, toward the enemy); past $B4 it is spent; its life counts down, and at 0 it is spent and marked landed ($8748; only the balls' marks are read, $A5D3).

each ball marked landed: the crater or the bridge's damage ($A6A5); then every object with a picture and standing, of either side, within 9 pixel pairs across and 8 lines up or down of where it landed, falls (counter 1); a cannon hit noted.
a cannon hit ($87A4, slot $87A5) of a person's side while it aimed: its gauge strip goes back ($8FC2).
charging rider X against the enemy's objects: one with a picture and standing within 4 pixel pairs across and 4 lines up or down of the rider falls; a cannon hit noted.

sound 15; on the canyon and the river, a ball that lands in the hazard (its row's column and the 5 after it) leaves no mark; one on a bridge row between columns 16 and 22 hits the bridge ($8262): the first two hits draw its damage (pictures 7 and 8 on the canyon at place 11, 10 and 11 on the river at place 12), the third breaks it (9 or 12, and $A794), later ones nothing; anywhere else, and anywhere on the open field, a crater (picture 14, or 13 on the canyon) at place 10, set to the cell below where it landed ($822E, $8248).
X kept by ball_crater: the operand of the ldx at $A791, written at $A781.
the bridge rows of both hazard tables ($8758-$875A, $8775-$8776) become the hazard (columns 17 and 16), so nothing crosses the broken bridge.
a person's side ($0382) with a territory to fall back to ($0390) presses its fall-back key ($8785: E for the Union, the up-arrow for the Confederacy): $A7C1.

unless either side has fallen back already, and while both still have infantry or cavalry: the side's infantry and cavalry fall back ($860E, $860C), $0392 marks it for the map, and both turn to their own edge ($8787: the Union left, the Confederacy right).

unless the side fell back: when none of its six soldiers is left on the field and it still has infantry ($038A), the next six march on ($A8E3, $9423); the same for its three riders ($9479); and when its cannon was hit and gone and cannons remain ($038E), the next one ($94DB).

whether a side is beaten ($A8B5) or has fallen back ($A891); once the battle is over ($87A6), every 100 frames ($86B8) the music fades ($F134 = 9, unless fading already) and after the third ($86B9, about four seconds) the battle ends ($80F9).
a side that fell back ($0392), once its infantry and cavalry have left: its cannons are lost ($038E, $8610 = 0), it is out ($0394 = $FF) and the battle is over ($87A6).
a side with no infantry or cavalry left and no cannon to fight with (none, or the last out of shots with none in reserve): it is out ($0394 = $FF, $0392 cleared, cannons 0) and the battle is over.
the eight lanes free again ($869A), before a new unit picks one.
sound A on the map's player ($F12B), only while the battle goes on ($86B9 still 3), with $A909 counted up so the interrupt does not play sound meanwhile; X and Y kept in the two ld operands.
Y kept by bat_sound: the operand of the ldy at $A901, written at $A8F1.
X kept by bat_sound: the operand of the ldx at $A903, written at $A8F4.
counted up while $A8EE starts a sound, so the interrupt does not play it meanwhile.
the open field's bitmap, packed (field 0): grass with a few patches of earth, short because it is mostly one colour; two bytes after the stream's end ($AAC0) are not read.
the open field's screen bytes, packed. The unpacker writes one byte more than it is asked for, so its last step reads on into $AB6E-$AB6F, the river's first bytes.

the river field's bitmap, packed (field 2): green grass, a winding blue river from top to bottom, a road across it on a stone bridge, and paths of earth; two bytes after the stream's end ($B9BA) are not read.
river_bitmap_pk, continued: bytes $ABAC-$AE2B of the block at $AB6E.
river_bitmap_pk, continued: bytes $AE2C-$AE85 of the block at $AB6E.
river_bitmap_pk, continued: bytes $AE86-$AF6D of the block at $AB6E.
river_bitmap_pk, continued: bytes $AF6E-$B36D of the block at $AB6E.
river_bitmap_pk, continued: bytes $B36E-$B76D of the block at $AB6E.
river_bitmap_pk, continued: bytes $B76E-$B9BC of the block at $AB6E.
the river field's screen bytes, packed; six bytes after the stream's end ($BBC0) are not read.
river_screen_pk, continued: bytes $BBA0-$BBC6 of the block at $B9BD.
the river field's colours, packed; two bytes after its end ($BD86) are not read.
river_colour_pk, continued: bytes $BBFA-$BC53 of the block at $BBC7.
river_colour_pk, continued: bytes $BC54-$BD88 of the block at $BBC7.
picture 0, 3 cells by 2: a house with a red roof (48 bytes of bitmap, 6 of screen, 6 of colour), scenery on the open field and the river.
pictures 7 to 9, each 9 cells by 5 (360 bytes of bitmap, 45 of screen, 45 of colour, from $BDC5, $BF87 and $C149): the canyon's wooden bridge after one hit, after two, and broken.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $BF10-$BF10 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $BF11-$BF13 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $BF14-$BF14 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $BF15-$BF17 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $BF18-$BF18 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $BF19-$C001 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: from $C000, the memory-map edge, inside picture 8 (the bridge after two hits), whose bitmap runs $BF87-$C0EE.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $C002-$C01C of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $C01D-$C037 of the block at $BDC5.
pic_canyon_bridge, continued: bytes $C038-$C052 of the block at $BDC5.

code nothing in the battle calls, left in memory when the file was saved: it keeps the registers ($CFD6-$CFDD) and, with the border and background grey, takes commands one byte at a time over the user port ($DD01, with handshakes on bit 2 and bit 3 of $DD00): $B4 bytes into memory, $B6 bytes out, $B5 a jsr to an address it is sent and $BA any three-byte instruction, each run with the kept registers, $B7 the $01 to use, $B8 and $B9 the registers out and in.
